title: Understand and Use Standard Deviation
description: Interpret standard deviation as spread, compare data sets conceptually, predict how changing values affects spread, and calculate standard deviation with Desmos.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep your first idea, even if you are unsure. You can continue without submitting an answer.

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html:
Data set A consists of the values \(42, 44, 45, 47\), and data set B consists of the values \(30, 40, 50, 60\). Which statement correctly compares the standard deviations of the two data sets?

  1. The standard deviation of data set A is less than the standard deviation of data set B.
  2. The standard deviation of data set A is greater than the standard deviation of data set B.
  3. The standard deviations are equal because both data sets contain four values.
  4. The standard deviations cannot be compared without knowing each data set's median.

blocks.html:
Compare spread instead of size

The opening sets have different values, but standard deviation asks how spread out they are. We can often compare that without a long calculation.

We’ll start with two pictures sharing the same mean so the difference in spread is easy to see.

Which picture spreads farther?

Both means are 10. Which set’s values typically lie farther from it?

figure.alt: Two dot plots with mean 10: Set A is clustered at 8 through 12, while Set B is spread from 2 through 18
figure.caption: Sets A and B.

content.prompt: Which set in the diagram should have the larger standard deviation?
choices: Set A, because its values are closer together
Set B, because its values are spread farther from the mean
The sets have equal standard deviations, because both means are \(10\)
There is not enough information unless every deviation is calculated
content.hint: Standard deviation is about spread. Compare how far the dots usually sit from the mean line.
content.explanation: Set B has the larger standard deviation because its values are typically farther from the mean.

blocks.html:
Use standard deviation as a spread measure

Standard deviation describes how spread out values are around their mean. Smaller values indicate tighter clustering; larger values indicate greater spread. It is never negative.

A shift does not change spread

The mean describes the center; standard deviation describes spread around that center. The lists [1,2,3] and [11,12,13] have different means but the same spread.

Center, Spread, Change

  1. Locate each set’s own mean.
  2. Compare how far its values spread around that mean.
  3. For a change, inspect the values that remain.

If the comparison is unclear, calculate both rather than deciding from the means or endpoints alone.

content.prompt: Which data set has the largest standard deviation?
content.hint: Ignore which set has the largest values. Compare how far each set spreads around its own center.
content.explanation: \([2,6,10,14,18]\) reaches farthest from its center. The other three sets have the same narrow five-number pattern shifted to different centers.

blocks.html:
Adding a value can change the spread

A value at the mean adds to the cluster; a very distant value stretches it. For [8,9,10,11,12], adding 30 creates much more spread than adding another 10.

Inspect the whole set after the change, since its mean can move too.

content.prompt: The data set is \([8,9,10,11,12]\). Which added value would most likely increase its standard deviation?
content.hint: The current set clusters around 10. Which choice would stretch the set farthest away?
content.explanation: Adding \(30\) creates a value far from the cluster, so the spread and standard deviation increase.

blocks.html:
Focus on what remains after removal

Removing a distant value can tighten a set. Removing a central value can leave a less concentrated set. Compare the remaining values around their new mean.

content.prompt: The data set is \([4,5,5,5,6,20]\). Which change will most clearly decrease its standard deviation?
choices: Remove one \(5\)
Remove \(4\)
Remove \(6\)
Remove \(20\)
content.hint: Which value is farthest from the main cluster near 5?
content.explanation: Removing \(20\) removes the farthest value and makes the remaining set much tighter.

blocks.html:
A replacement can tighten or stretch the set

For [3,4,5,6,20], replacing 20 with 7 removes the distant value and puts it near the cluster. The standard deviation decreases. If a change is less clear, calculate both versions.

content.prompt: The data set is \([3,4,5,6,20]\). What happens to its standard deviation if \(20\) is replaced by \(7\)?
choices: It decreases because the replacement moves toward the cluster
It increases, because \(7\) is greater than \(6\)
It stays the same because the number of values is unchanged
It drops to zero, because the outlier disappears
content.hint: Compare how far 20 and 7 sit from the main cluster near 5.
content.explanation: Replacing \(20\) with \(7\) pulls the extreme value toward the center, so the set becomes less spread out.

blocks.html:
Changing every value by the same amount is a shift

Adding or subtracting a constant from every value moves the mean by that amount too. Distances from the mean stay the same, so standard deviation stays the same.

content.prompt: Every value in a data set is decreased by \(7\). What happens to the standard deviation?
choices: It decreases by \(7\)
It increases by \(7\)
It stays the same
It becomes negative
content.hint: The center shifts by 7 too. Think about whether any distance from the center changes.
content.explanation: The entire set shifts together, so its spread and standard deviation stay the same.

blocks.html:
Zero spread means identical values

[7,7,7,7] has standard deviation 0 because every value equals the mean. If any value differs, there is some spread.

content.prompt: Which data set has standard deviation \(0\)?
content.hint: Zero spread means no value is different from any other value.
content.explanation: Every value in \([6,6,6,6]\) is identical, so every distance from the mean is zero.

shared_prompt.title: Data for direct and named-list entry

blocks.html:
Ask Desmos for a numerical result

Type stdev(2,3,4,5,6). Read the result, about 1.58. This command returns the sample standard deviation.

For a question explicitly treating the listed data as the entire population, use stdevp instead. Follow any command or definition the question specifies.

choices: Approximately \(0.71\)
Exactly \(2\)
Approximately \(1.58\)
Exactly \(4\)
content.hint: Read the decimal displayed below the stdev expression.
content.explanation: Desmos reports approximately \(1.58\). You can use the displayed decimal; you do not need the hand-calculation formula.

blocks.html:
Store a set you want to change

Enter A=[2,3,4,5,6], then stdev(A) on another row. Change the list once and its result updates. Use the same standard-deviation command when comparing two versions.

Predict, then compare the results

Compare C and D before reading their standard deviations. Then read stdev(C) and stdev(D) to check whether the change stretched or tightened the spread.

choices: Set D's values produce a larger mean than set C's values do
Replacing \(12\) with \(20\) moves one value farther from the cluster
Set D uses a different list letter in the calculator
Each replacement increases a set's standard deviation
content.hint: Compare the positions of the old value 12 and the new value 20 relative to the other four values.
content.explanation: The replacement stretches the set outward. The reason is distance from the cluster, not the list name or the fact that a replacement occurred.

blocks.html:
Choose reasoning or calculation

For a clear spread comparison, use Center, Spread, Change. When a number is requested or the effect is uncertain, enter the data in Desmos and use the appropriate standard-deviation command.

Return to the two data sets

Try the opening comparison again. Decide which set is more spread out around its own center.

content.prompt: Return to the opening question. What answer do you get now?
choices: The standard deviation of data set A is less than the standard deviation of data set B.
The standard deviation of data set A is greater than the standard deviation of data set B.
The standard deviations are equal because both data sets contain four values.
The standard deviations cannot be compared without knowing each data set's median.
content.hint: Compare how far values sit from each set’s own mean. A higher mean alone does not mean more spread.
content.explanation: Set A's values cluster within a few units of their mean, while set B's sit \(10\) or more away, so B has the larger spread. Equal counts do not make spreads equal, and Desmos stdev confirms: about \(2.1\) versus \(12.9\).
content.solution: Set A's values cluster within a few units of their mean, while set B's sit \(10\) or more away, so B has the larger spread. Equal counts do not make spreads equal, and Desmos stdev confirms: about \(2.1\) versus \(12.9\).

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html: Data set A consists of the values \(42, 44, 45, 47\), and data set B consists of the values \(30, 40, 50, 60\). Which statement correctly compares the standard deviations of the two data sets?

content.prompt: From memory: what does standard deviation measure, what makes it bigger, and how do you ask Desmos for it?
choices: Standard deviation measures spread from the mean; farther values decrease spread, and Desmos stdev can calculate it
Standard deviation measures spread from the median; values above the mean increase spread, and Desmos total can calculate it
Standard deviation measures the gap between the largest and smallest values; adding any value increases it, and Desmos mean calculates it
Standard deviation measures spread from the mean; farther values increase spread, and Desmos stdev can calculate it
content.explanation: You have it. Standard deviation describes spread around the mean. Reason about whether values move toward or away from the center, and use stdev in Desmos when you need the numerical value.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

content.prompt: The data set is \([0,10]\). The value \(5\), which is the mean, is added. What happens to the standard deviation?
choices: It decreases because the new value joins the center of the set
It increases because the set has more values
It stays the same because the old endpoints did not move
It becomes zero because the mean was added
content.explanation: Adding a value at the mean increases the concentration near the center, so the standard deviation decreases.

content.prompt: The data set is \([0,5,10]\). The center value \(5\) is removed. What happens to the standard deviation?
choices: It decreases because there are fewer values
It becomes zero because only two values remain
It stays the same because 0 and 10 did not change
It increases because only the two far-apart endpoints remain
content.explanation: Removing the central value leaves only the far-apart endpoints, so the remaining set is more spread out.

content.prompt: Use Desmos to find \(\operatorname{stdev}(1,2,3)\). What is the result?
content.explanation: Desmos returns \(1\). The calculator handles the computation; your job is to enter the data accurately and interpret the result.

content.prompt: Order the data sets from smallest standard deviation to largest standard deviation: P = \([5,5,5,5]\), Q = \([4,5,5,6]\), R = \([0,5,5,10]\).
choices: R, Q, P
Q, P, R
P, Q, R
P, R, Q
content.explanation: P has standard deviation 0, Q has a small spread around 5, and R has the largest spread.

content.html:
Read the Spread

Compare distances from each set’s own mean.
